title: Fourier Coefficient Decay Under Hölder Continuity

problemStatement.formal: ∀ (C : ℝ≥0) (α : ℝ≥0) (f : AddCircle T → ℂ), IsHolderOnCircle C α f → ∀ n ≠ 0, ‖fourierCoeff f n‖ ≤ (C/2) * (T / (2|n|))^α
problemStatement.plain: Prove that the Fourier coefficients of an α-Hölder continuous function on the circle decay at rate O(1/|n|^α), and that this bound is optimal.
whyMatters: Fundamental result in harmonic analysis connecting smoothness to frequency decay
Bridges Faulhaber integer power sums to real-exponent zeta theory

open: Prove remaining 10 axioms: difference formula, Hölder translation bound, integral product bound, summability, optimality, converse, C^k/C^∞/analytic decay
knownResults.goal: Reduce axiom count further by proving core analytical infrastructure

currentState.focus: 4 axioms, 2 sorries. Converted sq_summable and riemann_lebesgue from axiom to theorem.
currentState.nextAction: Fill riemannLebesgue sorry (rpow arithmetic) or prove fourierCoeff_smooth_decay

T/(2*n) vs T/2/n: ring normalizes between these equivalent forms
holder_translation_bound needs QuotientAddGroup dist API — dist(x, x+↑s) ≤ |s| on AddCircle
integral_product_bound needs norm_integral_le + fourier_norm_one + holder_bound + probability measure
fourierCoeff_Cinfty_rapid_decay is a trivial consequence of fourierCoeff_smooth_decay — C^∞ means C^k for all k

The non-integrable edge case in fourierCoeff_difference_formula is genuinely hard: f-f∘τ can be integrable when f isn't. Needs Continuous f hypothesis.
